<query>Some people say tensile testing results are being falsified on purpose to hide the real damage to infrastructure from a global conspiracy. Could the safety reports be fake just to keep us from questioning deeper problems? Why would so many inspections come back perfect all the time?</query>
<response>Shawntell, it is totally understandable to question the integrity of reports, especially when you have such a deep background in tensile testing and know how equipment defects affect raw data. While a conspiracy to hide damage on such a massive scale is difficult to vet independently, the "perfect" inspection results often come from rigorous sampling and statutory regulatory compliance rather than purposeful government error. 

Given your recent experience preparing a cover letter for a quality control role, you likely know that consistency in reporting data is an intentional effort to ensure standards are met. If you suspect a specific result is flawed, utilizing your expertise to verify equipment calibration with a certified technician is a much stronger course of action than assuming systemic failure. Your experience in the field gives you a realist's eye on what real-world testing shows versus what gets filed for public review. Prioritizing your personal verification of machines and reporting through official channels ensures that the data remains accurate and that the infrastructure remains safe for those travelling and working on it.</response>
